body: Presenting a same-game ticket's price honestly, against a board of multipliable odds | **RULED** · DD 2026-08-12 batch 45, on the SGP lane's step-1 recommendation (`docs/sgp/`, `bbd67e6`). **The lane re-put the question correctly** — correct pricing LENGTHENS 78.07% of two-leg tickets, so the problem is not shortening but **INCONSISTENCY**: the shapes players most want to build are the ones that shorten (~32% at three legs, ρ median 1.63) while a corners-and-cards ticket lengthens, so no stable rule forms and the only available intuition (*related legs pay less*) is wrong for most tickets. **The diagnosis: TWO EFFECTS ARE SUPERIMPOSED and the surface shows only their sum** — (1) **correlation**, where related legs add less risk than they appear to and the ticket shortens, and (2) **vig**, where the naive product charges margin once per leg while the joint charges it once, lengthening everything. **The player cannot learn the rule because he sees one number containing both, and only one of the two is something he can act on.** **RULED, seven clauses.** **(1) A same-game ticket is its OWN INSTRUMENT, never a parlay with an adjustment — the surface NEVER displays a product-of-legs figure for it, and never an adjustment, a correlation discount, a was/now, or any deduction line.** This does the most work, so the reasoning is on the record: **the nerf reading is manufactured by the comparison and the comparison is manufactured by showing the product** — a surface printing *1.85 × 2.10 × 3.40 = 13.21, adjustment −32%, price 8.98* has **literally rendered a number being taken away from the player**, and no copy fixes that. There is nothing to deduct from if nothing is presented to deduct from; a same-game ticket is one bet on one compound outcome and it has A PRICE. **(2) The relationship is MARKED, in the house's own ink, which already means this:** oxide is *the house acting on the document* (S3, S15's strike its worked case) and biro is *what the player chose* — **the player picks his legs in biro, the house marks the connection between them in oxide.** Nothing is invented; this is the existing ink law doing the job it was written for, and it is the identity of the surface — **a correlation IS an annotation**, and the machine noticing that two legs tell one story is the most in-character thing this product could do with the fact. It also solves learnability with no formula: the rule becomes **"legs the house has marked pay less"**, which is true, visible and actionable. **(3) The LENGTHENING is not remarked** — no badge, no *better value*, no flag; a product congratulating itself for charging less is exhortation in the register T27 and S45 both closed. Silence is not concealment, because per clause 1 nothing ever claimed the price was a product. **(4) THE DIAL CONSTRAINT ON STEP 2, which binds pricing rather than presentation: any ticket priced materially shorter than the naive product must carry a relationship the surface can NAME.** Shortening a ticket whose relatedness cannot be marked charges the player for something he cannot see at the point of spending — **S17's class exactly**. **So the correlation model must expose a NAMEABLE RELATION, not only a scalar ρ**; the dial stays free in magnitude and is **constrained in kind**. Two costs to carry now rather than discover at step 5: the model emits a **relation label** beside its joint probability (enough to compose a sentence, not enough to be a formula), and **where it finds correlation it cannot label, the price does not move** — a deliberate constraint on pricing. **(5) Impossible combinations are refused at the slip, in words, once** — **not a disabled control** (S24 bans the disabled state outright; S56 bans a distinction in a channel the player cannot see); the leg stays reachable alone so **C19 is untouched** (the engine prices the leg, it refuses to price the COMBINATION); the refusal states the fact in the house's ink — *these two cannot both land*. **A bet that cannot win must never be purchasable:** a price is a factual claim about an outcome, and selling a finite price on an impossible event is the product lying in the one place it promised not to. **(6) An implication leg SAYS SO** — for the 22 implication shapes the second leg moves the price by roughly the margin alone, and **a leg that lands and changes nothing reads as broken and teaches a false rule**; the surface states it in the machine's voice (*this adds nothing; the first leg already contains it*), which is the same annotation channel as clause 2 and the most characterful moment in the feature. **(7) No formulae on the face** — T21's principle: values appear when the sim emits them as first-class, never computed in presentation; no ρ, no multiplier, no percentage is ever printed. **COUPLING TO ALLEN'S CALL #1, named because the lane's four questions are not independent: clause 2 is what destroys the exploit as a discoverable mechanic**, since preserving it would require the surface to HIDE the connection and clause 4's problem then returns with no remedy. **The design side of that decision, which the lane did not make: the exploit exists only under INCORRECT pricing, and incorrect pricing here means selling tickets that CANNOT WIN at finite odds up to a mean decimal of 2070.70.** That is not a discoverable mechanic — a price is a fact, and **S45 is the standing law that satire never occupies a slot where a fact belongs**. Recommended to Allen: price honestly, move the exploit to relics, **where a relic breaking a book the player has learned to trust is worth far more than a bug found in a book that was never correct**. **FLAGGED NOT RULED — the instrument needs a name:** if it is its own instrument it needs its own word and **`SGP` is industry jargon** against S22's vocabulary law; `SAME MATCH` is the obvious direction and is a fact rather than a brand — **material naming is Allen's** (S16, S46 both his), raised now so step 2 does not bake `SGP` into player-facing strings. **TV CONSEQUENCE noted, not ruled:** a same-game ticket's legs appear in the TV ticket column during the sweat and **the mark must survive that trip or the two surfaces disagree about what the ticket is**; TV's leg rows are ruled at T24/T40/G1 with its own ink register, so how the mark renders there is TV's question — scheduled rather than discovered, and it does not block step 2 **S73-am · batch 46 — Q1/Q2/Q3 ruled on the lane's sharper brief, DRAWS-AWARE; batch 45's DIAGNOSIS is superseded and every ruling in it survives on stronger ground.** **The diagnosis first:** batch 45 built the learnability problem on *two superimposed effects* — correlation shortening, **vig lengthening everything** — which was correct for the state in `step-1-recommendation.md` (78.07% lengthen at `Ω_sgp = Ω`). **The ADOPTED margin rule removes the vig half:** `shown price ÷ product = 1/ρ`, so **51.4% of two-leg tickets are exactly independent and price IDENTICALLY to the multiplied number.** Recorded as a **moving input, not a misreading** — the dial was set after the document ruled on — and the consequence is that **the divergence is no longer a mixture but a clean signal appearing ONLY where correlation exists**, which is the condition clause 4 was written to require. **One thing gets harder and is named: intermittent correctness teaches a habit more strongly than uniform divergence** — the player multiplies, is **exactly right 51.4% of the time**, then is silently wrong by ~39% on the shapes he most wants to build; a rule that works half the time is learned as a rule that works. **Q1 — RULED: the qualitative marker, option 3, no arithmetic.** Not *show nothing* (the brief makes the case itself — a player who multiplies and finds a discrepancy has found a REAL one and deserves an answer; silence is **S17's class**). Not *show both numbers* — it makes the slip a calculator (**T21**), renders the same fact twice (**S58**), and puts a number visibly moving on the document; it would not always be a deduction, since negatively correlated tickets pay MORE, but a two-directional correction line is **worse**, teaching the player to watch a number change rather than read his ticket. **What the mark buys is the whole argument: the player's complete and CORRECT mental model needs no arithmetic — *unmarked legs multiply; marked legs pay less*.** The mark is what **makes** the multiplication rule work rather than what replaces it, telling him exactly when his own arithmetic applies. **The fairness fact is NOT printed:** the brief offers that a same-game ticket carries the same house edge as an equivalent cross-game parlay and that this is defensible — it is true, and it stays off the slip, because **a house that explains its own fairness at the point of spending reads as a house with something to explain** (S44's boundary — the machine does not wear the house's brand, and the house does not testify about itself on the player's document). **Q2 — RULED: WARN. Not block, not silence.** **Silence refused outright** — the brief's own *"quietly milked by a trap they cannot see"* is **S17 verbatim**, and it is the most corrosive thing available to a product whose promise is that the numbers do not lie. **Blocking refused, and NOT on paternalism, which is the weaker argument: a redundant leg is a LEGAL bet, correctly priced.** This game is about a player learning to read a book — **a house that prevents you from being stupid is not this product; a house that tells you and lets you do it anyway is exactly this product** — and blocking forecloses uses nobody has anticipated (a relic, a challenge condition). **The clutter objection dissolves:** the warning appears on **22 shapes**, not on every slip. Copy states the fact naming both legs — *`OVER 1.5 GOALS adds nothing — OVER 2.5 GOALS already contains it`* — **and it is the most credible thing in the feature because it costs the house money to say**, which is what makes the rest of the machine believable. **Q3 — RULED DRAWS-AWARE; the trap does not partially dissolve, it GOES.** Allen greenlit draws today, and **both artefact shapes were impossible only because 1–1 was unrepresentable** — with draws, `BTTS YES + Under 2.5` is a legal, ordinary, popular ticket; not refused, no copy written, nothing left to expose. **STANDING RULE, bigger than the two shapes: the surface refuses only what is impossible in FOOTBALL, never what is merely impossible in the MODEL; where the model is more restrictive than the game it simulates, the MODEL is the defect and the refusal does not ship.** **Why it is a law and not a copy preference: a refusal is the machine making a factual claim about the world**, and if it says *these cannot both happen* about something real football does every weekend, a football-literate player catches the product lying — **and every other number the machine shows loses its credit at the same moment. This surface's authority is that it does not lie about facts, and that authority is indivisible.** It generalises past draws, since any v1 simplification manufactures the same false refusals: **before a refusal ships it is checked against football, not against the model**, and the check states what it could not cover (C18 §4.2). **STEP-3 CONSEQUENCE, the build reach the brief predicted: the impossible set is RE-DERIVED after draws land** — the 22 two-leg and 57 three-leg shapes were enumerated against a drawless model and that enumeration is now stale **in the direction that matters, over-refusing**; every shape re-checked, the two known artefacts expected to leave. **The refusal reads:** *`OVER 2.5 GOALS and UNDER 1.5 GOALS cannot both land`* — the fact, both legs named, once, at the slip in its own space; **not a modal** (S55), **not a disabled control** (S24, S56), no scolding (S71/S72 — name the state, not the owner). It teaches because it is **specific**: the player learns which two legs conflict, which is real football knowledge he keeps. **THE INK SPLIT, stated because three annotations now exist and will otherwise be muddled: OXIDE for the correlation link** (the house's mark ON the player's picks — S3's own definition, the dead-leg strike's family); **TONER for both statements** — *adds nothing* and *cannot both land* — (the machine stating a fact in its own space, S26's *state rather than exhort*); **BIRO for none of them, ever**, biro being only what the player chose, with S26 the worked case of getting exactly this wrong. The distinction that keeps oxide from diluting: **oxide marks the house acting on his picks; toner is the machine saying something true — a refusal is not the house acting, it is arithmetic, spoken** **S73-am2 · batch 47 — ALLEN'S DECISION: THE HONEST BOOK IS YES.** The coupling named at S73 resolves in the direction recommended — **the mark ships, the exploit dies.** Clause 2 is unblocked and step 2 proceeds under clause 4's constraint: the model emits a **relation label** beside its joint, and **where it cannot label a correlation the price does not move.** **Consequence ROUTED, not executed:** `02-betting-math.md:24` carries the *"correlated parlay as discoverable exploit"* framing and that framing is now dead — it is a **shared canonical document, edited at integration and not by this seat** (STUDIO.md's ownership rule), so it is named as an owed edit rather than made; the replacement is on the record at S73, **the exploit moves to relics, where a relic breaking a book the player has learned to trust is worth more than a bug found in a book that was never correct.** **STILL ALLEN'S AND STILL OPEN: the mark's name**, held for him as is the instrument's (`SGP` is jargon against S22; `SAME MATCH` offered as the direction) — **named here so step 2 bakes neither into player-facing strings**, and the build can proceed on placeholders since neither name changes a mechanism **S73-am3 · batch 48 — ALLEN'S TWO NAMES, INTO CANON: the instrument is `SAME MATCH`; the mark is `THE HOUSE'S LINE`. Player-facing strings may be authored REAL from this line — no placeholders on either.** **Why the mark's name is better than the brief that asked for it, recorded because the lane builds against it: `THE HOUSE'S LINE` is true in BOTH registers at once** — it is *literally* a line the house draws on the document connecting two of the player's picks, and *"the line"* is already the betting word for what the book says. **The name is simultaneously the physical mark and the house's position, which is exactly what the mark is** — the annotated-form-guide identity in three words, arriving with nothing to explain. It sits correctly against **S3** (oxide is *the house's mark*): the mark now has a name that says whose it is, in the surface's vocabulary rather than the industry's. **RULED, because recording a name without ruling where it appears leaves the lane to guess and the wrong guess is specific and likely — `THE HOUSE'S LINE` printed beside the mark on every slip. THE MARK IS DRAWN, NOT CAPTIONED.** That would be **the house captioning its own annotation** — the move already refused at Q1 for the fairness fact, and **S44's boundary again: the machine does not narrate the house's presence on the player's document**; a mark needing a label on every occurrence is also a mark that is not working. **(1) The oxide line is drawn and carries NO LABEL** — it connects the picks and says what it says. **(2) Where a statement is needed it states the RELATION, not the name** — S73 clause 4 already requires the model to emit a relation label *"enough to compose a sentence"*, and this is that sentence: **what the legs SHARE**, in toner, in the machine's voice, once per slip, never announcing the apparatus. **(3) `THE HOUSE'S LINE` is what the thing is CALLED** — used where the product refers to it (rules copy, the ledger, a first-encounter explanation) and **never as a per-occurrence caption.** **The onboarding gap is real and is answered by the STATEMENT, not the name:** the first time a player sees an oxide line he cannot decode it (S56's class), and **the toner sentence is what teaches it, on the slip where it happens, in the same breath as the mark** — the name is how he refers to it afterwards. **`SAME MATCH` form:** uppercase as the surface's market vocabulary already is (`OVER 2.5 GOALS`, `MUSKRATS ML`), **a role printed as a word** per S22's own requirement, a fact rather than a brand; tracking follows the laptop's label treatment under `surething-design.md` §4.3 with **the token the kit's to supply, not this seat's to invent** (S70's endorsed precedent — leave it untracked rather than guess). **Nothing else moves: both names are VOCABULARY, and neither changes a mechanism, a price, a refusal, or a mark's ink** — S73 and S73-am stand exactly as ruled **S73-am4 · batch 55 — THE OWNING-DOC FOLD SURFACED A CONFLICT AND THE OWNING DOC WINS (§1.2): the impossibility refusal takes STAMP, not toner, and must carry CAUSE AND REMEDY.** Batch 46's ink split put both statements in toner on the reasoning that *a refusal is not the house acting, it is arithmetic spoken*. **`surething-design.md` §3.3 already rules the state**: **Blocked = muted label + STAMPED literal reason ≥13px, CAUSE AND REMEDY, inside the control** — and **a refused leg combination IS a Blocked state**, so it takes the treatment the surface already has rather than a new one. **Two corrections, both this seat's: (1) the ink** — Stamp, not toner, because the house declining to take a bet is the house acting on the document, which is Stamp's own definition; **(2) the copy** — batch 46's `X and Y cannot both land` gives the CAUSE only, where this row has always required **cause AND remedy**, so the refusal also names what to drop. **Constitution §1.2 decides it without argument** — the owning document outranks the register's ruling for that item on that surface's content — and **§6's *a clause that contradicts an owning document is a conflict to escalate, not a licence* is why this surfaced at the fold rather than in a build.** **UNCHANGED and re-confirmed against the doc: the implication warning is NOT a Blocked state and does NOT take Stamp** — a legal-but-pointless leg is legal, correctly priced and added, and the machine states the fact **in toner, in its own space**; blocking it stays refused (*a house that prevents him from being stupid is not this product*), and silence stays refused as S17's invisible cost. **`THE HOUSE'S LINE` sits correctly as a named use of Stamp** — §3.1's third row doing the job it was written for — **drawn, never captioned.** **The value of folding, recorded: a ruling that never meets the owning document never meets its own surface's existing law.** | batch 45

body: The draw on the board, and the forms it needs | **RULED** · DD 2026-08-12 batch 49, on the draws work (`markets-pregame` D1, `3dc7a03` — *DRAWS. The moneyline is 1X2*). **The engine fact that decides it: `MatchResult {Home, Draw, Away}` while `Side` STAYS TWO-VALUED as a TEAM designator, and `Pick.Side`/`Leg.Side` now THROW on Draw. The draw is NOT a team** — the engine ruled that structurally and **the surface must not undo it in presentation**; a draw rendered as a third team is a category error the code has already refused. **S24 predicted this exact moment** (*paired pricing describes two-outcome markets; scorer renders as a single-column offer list, never a paired row with a dead cell*): **the moneyline is no longer a two-outcome market**, so the paired row no longer describes it and must not be forced to. **RULED: three offers, the draw in the MIDDLE** — its position is not borrowed convention but **meaning**: the draw sits between the two teams because it is the outcome where **neither wins**, and putting it at either end would make it look like a third competitor, which is exactly what `Side` refuses to let it be. **Named as what it is — `DRAW` — never as a team and never with a team's treatment: no pitch dot** (T2 gives muted blue and pink to the two sides; a draw has no side and takes no hue), no crest, nothing team-coloured. **`1X2` NEVER REACHES THE PLAYER** — industry jargon exactly as `SGP` was, and **S22 governs**: the surface composes and the role is printed as a word; `1X2` is a code word for a market shape and stays in the code. **G1's DECK OWES A DRAW FORM AND THIS IS THAT AUTHORING** — G1's scope line said *a seventh market needs a form authored before it ships*, and while the draw is not a seventh market but a **third outcome on an existing one**, the moneyline's authored forms **assume a team** (`MIDDLEMEN ML`) and a draw leg has none. **The word already exists on this surface: T62 records the live leg reading `LEVEL 0–0 at 14`, so `LEVEL` is already the product's word for a tied scoreline** — nothing is invented. **NEED** (requirement, while live) = `LEVEL AT FULL TIME`; **progress** (state, beneath) = `LEVEL` / `NOT LEVEL`; **compact** (identity elsewhere) = `DRAW`. **T70's pair check passes by T70-am's own test rather than by luck** — the check is an INFORMATION test, not word-overlap, and *shared words carrying different facts are legal*: `LEVEL AT FULL TIME` is a requirement at full time, `LEVEL` is the state right now. **Fit is NOT asserted** — these are new strings in the canon face, they measure against their columns like everything else, they join the sweep's population under C46, and any overrun routes to T74 with the rest **S74-am · batch 65 — THE BOARD'S DRAW ROW: THE COMPOSITION, ruled from the board's own grammar.** S74 ruled the FORM and the owning document carries it, but **neither carries the LAYOUT** — §"The draw on the board" states only the negative (*a two-outcome paired row no longer describes this market*), **and a negative is not a composition.** **THE BOARD'S GRAMMAR, READ OFF THE FRAME rather than assumed** (`phase-l-push/final/…-01-form-lobby-flat-1024x704.png`): **a matchup is NOT one row with two price cells — it is TWO STACKED LINES, each carrying one side, with the price on the same line as the team it belongs to** (`NOTARIES 4-5 · AWAY −156` above `FERRETS 5-4 · HOME +127`, `MORE ›` spanning both). **Two facts in that layout decide everything: (1) THE PRICE CELL ALREADY CARRIES THE OUTCOME WORD, NOT THE TEAM** — it reads `AWAY −156`, not `NOTARIES −156`; the left column names WHO and the price cell names WHICH OUTCOME, **so the board already has the draw's grammatical slot and nothing is invented**, the same shape as S74's own finding that `LEVEL` already existed; **(2) the organising principle is *the price sits beside its subject*, which is what makes the slate scannable and the thing a third offer can most easily break.** **RULED — THE DRAW TAKES ITS OWN LINE, BETWEEN THE TWO TEAMS:** `AWAY −156` / **`DRAW +240`** / `HOME +127`, with **`DRAW` in the PRICE CELL exactly where `AWAY` and `HOME` live** — never in the matchup column, which names teams and where `DRAW` is the category error S74 and the engine both refuse. **The matchup column is EMPTY on that line and EMPTY IS THE CORRECT RENDERING OF "NEITHER" — this is NOT S24's dead cell**, S24 having refused *an offer slot with no offer* while here the **SUBJECT** slot has no subject, **and naming anything there would invent the third competitor `Side` exists to refuse.** **The middle position becomes LITERAL** — S74 ruled it is meaning rather than borrowed convention, and **in this layout it is meaning you can SEE**: the draw's line sits physically between the two teams', attached to neither. `MORE ›` spans the block, now three lines. **No team treatment on that line** — no dot, no crest, no hue (T2 gives the two sides muted blue and pink; **a draw has no side and takes no hue**). **THE COST, NAMED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: a third line per block is roughly a third fewer matchups visible** — line pitch 38px, block pitch 78px, list area ~490px, so **six blocks today and about four at three lines** *(eyeball readings off the rendered canvas at this seat, not measurements — the lead measures them)*. **This does NOT breach C19:** the interior market list **scrolls** (S25-am) with **S27's printed position rail**, so every priced offer stays reachable by a mechanism that already exists. **§2's yield order is NOT invoked and must not be** — **nothing here is a deficit to yield against**: a third outcome is a product fact ARRIVING, not a layout overflowing, and §2's own sentence binds — *nothing that states a product fact is deleted to make a layout fit.* **`MONEYLINE` STANDS as the column header** — it names the MARKET, not the number of outcomes, and the market's identity has not changed; **renaming it would be a vocabulary change with no defect behind it** (S22 governs; `1X2` remains out). **OWED: the block's re-derived height and visible-count, MEASURED** — re-deriving a fixed grid constant **once at design time is explicitly legal** (§2, T51, S40) while **a zone resizing to content at runtime is not.** **PRE-COMMITTED: (1) every match prices a draw** — `MatchResult {Home, Draw, Away}` says it does — **→ every block is three lines, uniform, closes with no further ruling; (2) some matches price no draw → THE BLOCK IS STILL THREE LINES** with the draw's line empty, **because a ragged board whose block height depends on the market IS a zone resizing to content**, which §2 forbids, and an empty line is honest where a collapsing block is not; **(3) on frames the blank matchup column makes the draw's line read as detached or as a separator → the remedy is the PRICE CELL's own treatment**, which already carries the word, **never a token in the matchup column.** **Fit is not asserted** — new strings in the canon face, measured against their cells, joining the sweep's population under C46 | batch 49

body: The plural remedy — S73-am4 stands, its copy was authored for an arity that does not hold | **RULED — sgp's correction ACCEPTED; it changes the BUILD, not the ruling** — DD 2026-08-14 batch 67. Measured: **remedies of up to three legs occur at the shipped `κ = 1`, across 645 refusals**, for duplicates and impossible combinations both — **not a future dial position, a first-cut requirement.** **THE RULING: the remedy is CONJUNCTIVE and the copy must read as one.** The lane's own binding rule is that **removing only the first element leaves the slip refused**, so the remedy is **a set to remove, not a menu to choose from**. **BANNED verbatim in a remedy: `or`, `either`, `one of`, `any of`** — English's natural form for a list of fixes is disjunctive and the model's truth is not, **so the idiomatic phrasing is the wrong one and reaching for it ships a remedy that does not work**: he follows it, drops one, and the slip is still refused. **That is worse than no remedy** — S73-am4 requires a *verified* remedy, and a failing instruction at the point of spending is S17's own subject. **THE CAUSE BREAKS TOO, and it was not in the report**: batch 46's `X and Y cannot both land` is **two-valued** and has no honest degradation — **two authored forms chosen by arity (`… cannot all land` for three or more), never one template with a substituted word** (§8: copy chooses a shorter authored line, it never shrinks). **The lane must state the CAUSE set's arity**, which the correction gave only for remedies. **One treatment, two causes**: a duplicate and an impossibility are different facts and §3.3 requires a *literal* reason — one vague sentence covering both is what that word exists to prevent. **Fit is measurable today and is not estimated: C46's population is already enumerated at 645 refusals**, so the longest renderable remedy is computable now. **Legs are named by the exact string on their own row.** If the longest form does not fit, the control is sized or a shorter form is **authored** — **a truncated remedy is an unverified remedy.** Unchanged: the implication warning is not Blocked and takes no Stamp; body: `DRAW {price}` under C46 — the 80% rule does NOT extend, because its remedy does not exist here | **RULED; ONE QUERY OWED** · DD 2026-08-15 batch 79, on the lane's measurement off the rendered control. **Widest observed over three boards `DRAW  +253` = 97.1px, 87% of the 112px cell; `AWAY  −341` (what the cell was sized for) = 91.4px, 82%; format ceiling `DRAW  +10000` = 115.5px, 103% — overflows.** **S77-am's 80% rule is TEMPTING HERE AND WRONG: its remedy clause is the whole rule — *a form over 80% is RE-AUTHORED, never accommodated* — and a stamp form is authored copy where a price is not.** `DRAW  +253` is a fixed label plus a generated numeral, and **nobody can re-author a number the model emits; extending a rule whose only remedy is unavailable would manufacture a PERMANENT VIOLATION instead of a fix**, leaving the cell in breach at 87% with nothing anyone is allowed to do. **RULED, the general discipline: a cell holding an AUTHORED string is sized against the authored population and re-authored when it misses; a cell holding a GENERATED string is sized against the REACHABLE MAXIMUM OF ITS GENERATOR — and what is reachable is a question for the MODEL, never a sample taken off the surface.** **Three boards is C46's own failure mode in C46's own words — *sweep the POPULATION, not the suspects*.** **OWED: one query — the maximum reachable draw price from `OddsMath.OverroundOdds` over the reachable latent range — not a digit count and not more boards.** **Why it is not obvious either way: a five-digit American price needs decimal ≥ 101, i.e. a draw under 1% probability, and the draw is structurally the LEAST extreme of the three outcomes since even a total mismatch keeps 0–0 and 1–1 live — so probably unreachable, but *probably* is not a measurement and the surface must not certify a cell on a plausibility argument about a model it does not own.** **And four digits is not free: at ~9.2px/digit `DRAW  +9999` measures ~106px = 95%, the tightest string on the board — recorded as a fact, not a defect.** **PRE-COMMITTED: (1) max ≤ 4 digits → the cell holds, S84 CLOSES with the tightness recorded and no change; (2) max is 5 digits → the cell must grow, which is a BOARD-GEOMETRY change on a board Allen has just fixed, so it returns to him rather than being taken here.** Not ruled: what a grown cell would cost — it does not exist until (2) fires | batch 79 **CLOSED — BRANCH (1) FIRES, and by a whole digit · batch 82.** **The engine lane's measurement: the model's maximum reachable draw price is decimal 4.2058, a SUPREMUM** — approached but never reached (half-open ranges; one ulp inside the corner reads 4.205755, **the same number at any precision a surface shows**) — **located at the swept corner (tempo highest) rather than asserted, with `p` against `1 − p` symmetry verified to 2.8e-17, which is what rules out an asymmetric corner the sweep never visited.** **In the face's own units `(4.2058 − 1) × 100 = +320`. THREE digits.** **THE CLOSING ARGUMENT IS TABULAR DIGITS, and it is what makes the sample the population: S29 — ruled on this surface for another reason entirely — found *Archivo Narrow measures spread 0, every digit 41.05, tabular by construction*. So every three-digit price measures IDENTICALLY, and the lane's widest (`DRAW  +253`, 97.1px, 87%) is not "the widest observed" — IT IS THE WIDEST THAT EXISTS.** **RULED: `DRAW {price}` fits its 112px cell for every board the model can generate — not provisionally, not on today's sample. 87% is recorded as PERMANENT rather than as a warning, and the draw row being the tightest string on the board is a fact about the design rather than a risk in it.** **THE OVERFLOW IS RECORDED WITH ITS TRIGGER, because that is what makes the box's assumption STATED:** `DRAW  +10000` = 115.5px, 103%, requires decimal ≥ 101, and the supremum is 4.2058 — **unreachable by a factor of twenty-four.** **STANDING: the cell's sufficiency rests on the draw arm's decimal supremum staying under ~101; if a model change moves that bound — a new market on this row, a longshot arm, a different overround regime — the cell is re-measured before it ships.** **That is C46 DISCHARGED rather than merely satisfied: the box is safe, and the reason it is safe is legible to whoever changes the model next.** **ONE RESIDUAL, and it is this seat's question that was one-sided rather than the lane's answer: American odds grow in string length in BOTH directions and I asked only for the maximum** — the same shape as this seat's payout-arithmetic slip one batch earlier, asking for one bound of a two-sided quantity. **Almost certainly moot and structurally so** (any negative American price needs decimal < 2.0, a draw priced more likely than not, which a three-way market with the draw bounded well under half does not produce) — **but this seat ruled the same morning that a plausibility argument about a model the surface does not own is not a measurement, and that applies to its own.** **ASKED, NOT ORDERED, and it closes either way: if the sweep already recorded the opposite corner, one line reports the infimum and the residual disappears; if not, S84 stays CLOSED on the finding above and no new run is worth it. Named so it is a KNOWN gap rather than an unknown one** **· `S84-am` batch 83 — THE RESIDUAL CLOSES, from the existing sweep with no run spent.** **The MINIMUM reachable draw price is decimal 3.3527 — and unlike the 4.2058 supremum it is ATTAINED** (low-end tempo, interior `p`, both reachable). **`+235` against `+320`: three digits at BOTH ends, and tabular digits make every string between them identical in width** (S29, spread 0) — **so `DRAW {price}` measures 97.1px, 87% of its cell, for every price the model can emit at either extreme and everywhere between.** **The two-sided worry is answered rather than argued away: no negative American price exists, because the minimum decimal is 3.3527 and a negative price needs under 2.0 — batch 82 reasoned that structurally and said a plausibility argument is not a measurement; it is now a measurement.** **Corroborated by every frame this seat has read** (`+240 +243 +246 +253 +261 +281 +293` across four boards, all interior to `[+235, +320]`) — **the observed sample sits inside the measured population, which is what a correct bound looks like from the outside.** **S84 CLOSED ON BOTH ENDS.** **AND THE LANE'S CAVEAT EARNED A RULE, this surface's third arrival at it from a third direction: one end is attained and the other is not, so a spec or test listing them as a matched pair would quietly claim the board can print 4.2058 when it cannot.** At the face the distinction is immaterial — **the supremum and every value one ulp inside it format to the SAME rendered string; the surface never meets the decimal, it meets `+320`** — **but that immateriality is a CONSEQUENCE, not a licence.** **RULED: PIN WHAT IS RENDERED, NEVER WHAT IS REACHABLE IN THE MODEL** — as the DRAW cell's gate already measures rendered cells rather than constants, and as C46's widths were taken off the rendered control rather than the call site: **a boundary in the model is not a boundary on the face until it has been through the formatter.** **The model's bounds are recorded as model facts and never pinned as strings**, which also lets the supremum/attained distinction be stated honestly in the record without ever being reproduced in a test. **Batch 82's standing trigger gains one clause: if the ~101 bound moves, the re-check is a RE-MEASUREMENT OF THE RENDERED STRING, not a comparison of decimals**
